We make it open. [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-Project_Homepage-2563EB?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D1117)](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/Paper-Tech_Report-B31B1B?style=flat-square&logo=arxiv&logoColor=white&labelColor=0D1117)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) [![Trajectories](https://img.shields.io/badge/Trajectories-Explore-6B52DF?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D1117)](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA/trajectories.html) [![macOS Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS_Harness-14%2B-7C5CFF?style=flat-square&logo=apple&logoColor=white&labelColor=0D1117)](#quick-start) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-22D3EE?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D1117)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join_us-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white&labelColor=0D1117)](#community) [![WeChat](https://img.shields.io/badge/WeChat-Group-07C160?style=flat-square&logo=wechat&logoColor=white&labelColor=0D1117)](#community) [News](#news) · [Results](#results) · [Demos](#demos) · **[Quick start](#quick-start)** · [SDK](#sdk) · [Open stack](#open-stack) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Contributing](#contributing) · [Contact](#contact)

**Computer use has reached a turning point.** GPT-6 Astra's demos offered an exciting vision of what computer-use agents could make possible, and the focus is expanding from GUI-only interaction to both visual and programmatic interfaces. The question has changed, from how well a model operates a GUI to how well a system completes work on a real computer by whatever means works. **We call such a system a generalist computer-use agent (GCUA).** It uses a computer in more ways than you do. It reads the accessibility tree and calls app APIs, runs shell commands, and operates the GUI when it needs to. With **code execution**, it writes GUI operations as code and combines them with all of these in one program, with loops and conditions. It can also share the computer with you, working in background windows without interrupting what you are doing. **Yet frontier systems remain largely closed.** We therefore introduce **Open Generalist CUA (OpenGCUA)**, an ongoing project to develop and open the full stack for GCUAs with the community, including model, system, trajectories, efficiency optimization, and evaluation. **What we open in this version:** - 🧠 **[OSWorld integration example](packages/harness/examples/osworld/)** with reference screenshot-action and code-action agents for integrating the OpenGCUA design. - 📜 **Evaluation trajectories** of the 8 frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, and Gemini 3.8 Flash. - 💻 **[macOS real-device harness](packages/harness/)** (preliminary), a menu-bar app that runs the agent on your own Mac. - 🔌 **[Cross-Device SDK](packages/sdk/)** (preliminary), one programming interface for computers, browsers, and phones. 🗺️ See the [detailed plan for our open stack](#open-stack). ## 🔥 News - **[2026-10]** 🚀 The OpenGCUA research preview is out, with the [tech report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200), the [OSWorld integration example](packages/harness/examples/osworld/), the [macOS real-device harness](packages/harness/), the [Cross-Device SDK](packages/sdk/), and evaluation trajectories of 8 frontier models. ## 📊 Results We test the design on two fronts: OSWorld-v2 with eight frontier models, and real Macs with our real-device harness. ![On the OSWorld-v2 offline set, OpenGCUA raises the partial score of all eight frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash (mean 45.3 to 64.9, +19.6 points), and cuts steps per task by 53% on average.](site/assets/readme/results-osworld.svg) - **Every model improves, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, and Gemini 3.8 Flash.** Over a GUI-only baseline with batched actions, the mean partial score rises from 45.3 to 64.9 (+19.6 points), and steps per task fall by 53% on average. GPT-6 Astra goes from 102 to 34 steps per task. - **Weaker models gain the most.** GLM-5.3-Flash gains 35.2 points and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 29.8. The gap between the strongest and the weakest model shrinks from 39.1 to 18.0 points. - **Code execution adds value beyond shell access.** With the same GUI and shell access, writing operations as code adds 6.1 points and cuts steps by 14.8% over a GUI+CLI agent (mean of three models). ![With the same real-device harness on four macOS tasks, Qwen3.8-Max uses 19.4 times the reasoning tokens of GPT-6 Astra per task and completes 3 of 4 tasks, while GPT-6 Astra completes 4 of 4.](site/assets/readme/results-real-device.svg) With our real-device harness held fixed, on four macOS tasks Qwen3.8-Max used 19.4 times the reasoning tokens of GPT-6 Astra and still completed fewer tasks. The case studies trace this gap to model behavior, which is what our next release, the GCUA model, works on. The [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22200) has the full setup, ablations, and case studies. ## 🎬 Demos Click a screenshot to watch the video. **One visa form, four workflows.** OpenGCUA, OpenGCUA (prefer GUI), GUI + batch, and Codex work on the same visa application on a real Mac. Playback speeds vary; use the in-video clocks for elapsed task time. [![OpenGCUA performing GUI actions on a visa form in macOS Preview.](site/assets/readme/demo-click-sequence.jpg)](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA-blog/demos/click-sequence.mp4) [▶ Watch the click sequence · 0:25](https://tongyi-mai.github.io/OpenGCUA-blog/demos/click-sequence.mp4) ## 🚀 Quick Start (macOS source harness) This is the shortest path from a clean clone to an interactive agent. It requires macOS 14+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Python 3.11–3.14, Rust/Cargo 1.89+, and Xcode Command Line Tools. Python 3.12 is recommended. Prebuilt SDK wheels do not require Rust. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Tongyi-MAI/OpenGCUA.git cd OpenGCUA uv venv --python 3.12 source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ./packages/sdk -e ./packages/harness/runtime # Install the native driver app. Its daemon is included in the app bundle. .venv/bin/mu setup macos .venv/bin/mu doctor macos .venv/bin/mu setup browser --engine chromium .venv/bin/mu doctor browser --engine chromium # Create a private local configuration from the shipped defaults. cp packages/harness/configs/macos_demo.json packages/harness/configs/local.json ``` Edit the following fields in `packages/harness/configs/local.json`: ```json { "api_key": "YOUR_API_KEY", "model_name": "qwen3.8-flash", "llm_base_url": "https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1", "llm_protocol": "openai" } ``` Keep the other fields copied from `macos_demo.json`; the object above shows only the values normally changed. Chat Completions-compatible gateways use `"llm_protocol": "openai"`; GPT reasoning endpoints with Responses support can use `"openai-thinking"` to replay encrypted reasoning across turns. Native Anthropic Messages endpoints use `"anthropic"`; set `"anthropic_thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}` in `local.json` for Claude models that support adaptive thinking. The Anthropic path preserves signed thinking blocks in subsequent requests; `reasoning_effort` is not an Anthropic thinking switch. Provider examples and every advanced setting are documented in [Setup, configuration, and troubleshooting](QUICKSTART.md). Grant **CuaDriver.app** access in **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility** and **Screen Recording**, quit and reopen CuaDriver, then verify the installation: ```bash .venv/bin/mu doctor macos ``` Start either the terminal agent or the browser demo studio. The terminal command automatically uses the visual interface when stdin/stdout are an interactive terminal; pipes and `TERM=dumb` keep the compatible plain-text interface. ```bash # Persistent visual terminal conversation. Type /exit or press Ctrl-D to stop. .venv/bin/python packages/harness/runtime/mac_agent.py # Force the original line-oriented output (also useful for scripts and logs). .venv/bin/python packages/harness/runtime/mac_agent.py --ui plain # Or start the demo studio at http://127.0.0.1:8800. bash packages/harness/runtime/start_demo.sh ``` In the visual terminal, reasoning and generated code are hidden by default. Use `/reasoning on` or `/code on` to show future output, `/help` for shortcuts, and Alt/Option+Enter to insert a newline. Ctrl-C during an active step aborts that turn; operations already sent to applications or the shell are not rolled back. If you see `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `DEVICE_OFFLINE`, a native-extension import error, or a recording problem, use the [error-indexed troubleshooting guide](QUICKSTART.md#troubleshooting). For SDK-only installation and wheel builds, see the [SDK guide](packages/sdk/README.md#install). The standalone [native macOS app](packages/macos/README.md) is a separate distribution path with its runtime bundled. ## Native macOS app [OpenGCUA for macOS](packages/macos/README.md) implements the menu bar assistant: enter a task, collapse into a floating control panel, reply to questions, and review saved results. SwiftUI + AppKit, with Python, the SDK and signed CuaDriver bundled inside the app; no browser or separately installed runtime is required. Apple Silicon / macOS 14+, currently a local development build. See the app guide for building, packaging and the remaining public-release validation. Version tags can automatically build the DMG and Python SDK downloads through GitHub Actions. ## 🔌 Cross-Device SDK The Cross-Device SDK is the interface the model programs against. It binds every operation to an explicit device, app, window, or tab, keeps accessibility and vision as separate ways to observe and act, and lets one program coordinate several devices in a task. ```python import asyncio from qwen_intelligence import Runtime async def main(): async with Runtime() as runtime: await runtime.add_macos(name="local-mac") async with runtime.session() as mu: mac = await mu.register("local-mac", name="mac") app = await mac.apps.get("com.apple.TextEdit") await mu.emit(await app.ui.ax.observe()) # TextEdit's accessibility tree await mu.emit(await app.windows.list()) asyncio.run(main()) # open TextEdit first ``` It has adapters for macOS, Android, browsers, and Linux, built on a Rust core with Python bindings. The [source setup above](#quick-start) installs it. The package is `qwen-intelligence-sdk`, imported as `qwen_intelligence` (`mai_ui` is the same API under its internal name). See [`packages/sdk/`](packages/sdk/) and the [examples](packages/sdk/examples/src/). ## 🗺️ The open stack and what comes next OpenGCUA aims to open the full stack of generalist computer use. This preview releases the first layers, and the rest come next. ![The full open stack. Model: a GCUA model for both computer use and browser use, next. Agent design: the OpenGCUA harness for OSWorld-v2 with code execution and harness-to-model decision transfer, released. Real device: the macOS real-device harness, a menu-bar app, and the Cross-Device SDK, both preliminary. Trajectory: execution trajectories of 8 frontier models including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash, released. Efficiency: execution efficiency through code execution, thinking length, harness design, and system-level improvements, next. Evaluation: real-device environments and a benchmark, next.](site/assets/readme/stack.svg) - [x] [OSWorld integration example](packages/harness/examples/osworld/) with standalone screenshot-action and code-action agents - [x] macOS real-device harness and Cross-Device SDK, as preliminary open-source versions - [x] [Native OpenGCUA macOS app](packages/macos/README.md), a preview menu-bar assistant with a floating task panel, voice, and bundled harness, SDK, and driver - [ ] **GCUA model** for both computer use and browser use, turning code execution, on-demand observation, and task tracking into learned skills - [ ] **Execution efficiency**, an essential problem for computer use: optimizing code execution, thinking length, and harness design, and exploring broader system-level improvements - [ ] **Real-device environments and benchmark**, macOS first, measuring useful work under real conditions - [ ] **Reliable work on your devices**: tasks across computers, browsers, and phones, with dependable targeting, recovery from failures, and continuity when you step in We do not commit to dates. The plan follows the evidence and what the community proposes, including directions beyond this list. Details are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## 🧩 How it works Formally, a GCUA is an agent system that completes diverse computer tasks through visual interaction and programmatic access, choosing **how to observe, act, and organize its work** as each task requires. These are three decisions made at every step. A GUI agent leaves all three to fixed rules in its harness. OpenGCUA lets the model make them. | Decision | GUI agent | OpenGCUA | |:--|:--|:--| | 👁️ **What to observe** | a screenshot after every action | `screenshot()`, only when the model needs one | | ✋ **How to act** | one click or keystroke at a time | a Python program that combines the accessibility tree and app APIs, shell commands, and GUI actions, with loops, branches, and checks | | 🗂️ **How to organize work** | fixed by the harness | the model keeps a `todo` list and states its `` before each program | Two designs make this work. **Code execution** lets a model bring the programming skill it already has, and lets intermediate results decide the next operation without another model call. **Harness-to-model decision transfer** moves choices such as when to look and what to track out of harness rules and into the model. GUI agents, CLI agents, and GUI+CLI hybrids such as our earlier Qwen-UI-Agent are special cases that fix some of these decisions in advance. Here is one real step by GPT-6 Astra on a CRM task in OSWorld-v2. Lines marked `...` are cut, and long lines are wrapped: ```python Apply the 29 evidence-based status changes while preserving all original customer details. todo.update(id="updates", kind="task", content="Applying 29 reviewed status changes ...", status="attempted") r = bash(r"""... cat > /tmp/apply_lead_statuses.py <<'PY' ... current=api(p,'/api/crm/workspace')['workspace'] assert current==original,'Workspace changed since original review; stopped before edits.' for change in changes: d=api(p,'/api/crm/leads/'+change['leadId'],'PATCH',{'status':change['to']}) ... assert lead['status']==change['to'] ... print('VERIFIED:',len(log),'status changes; all 40 statuses correct; ...') PY python /tmp/apply_lead_statuses.py""") if r.ok: todo.update(id="status_updates", kind="task", content="Applied and API-verified all 29 planned status changes. ...", status="claimed_verified") ``` In one step, the model states its intent and records its plan. It then writes and runs a script that stops if the app changed since it last looked, applies 29 edits through the app's own API, and checks each one. Only after the script succeeds does it record the result as verified. ## 🤝 Contributing We hope the community will shape not only how GCUAs are built, but also what they should be able to do and how progress is measured. There are three ways to join: - **Improve the harness and SDK.** Platform adapters, more reliable observation and control, faster execution, real-device testing, and documentation. - **Build real-device evaluation.** Environments, realistic tasks, evaluation criteria, and benchmark tooling, including traces that show where today's agents fail. - **Propose research goals.** Workflows agents should handle, capabilities worth building, or questions to study with the released code and trajectories.      Title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills 
     Authors: Yifan Yang ,  Ziyang Gong ,  Weiquan Huang ,  Qihao Yang ,  Ziwei Zhou ,  Zisu Huang ,  Yan Li ,  Xuemei Gao ,  Qi Dai ,  Bei Liu ,  Kai Qiu ,  Yuqing Yang ,  Dongdong Chen ,  Xue Yang ,  Chong Luo              View a PDF of the paper titled SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills, by Yifan Yang and 13 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Agent skills today are hand-crafted, generated one-shot, or evolved through loosely controlled self-revision, none of which behaves like a deep-learning optimizer for the skill, and none of which reliably improves over its starting point under feedback. We argue the skill should instead be trained as the external state of a frozen agent, with the same discipline that makes weight-space optimization reproducible. SkillOpt is, to our knowledge, the first systematic controllable text-space optimizer for agent skills: a separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits on a single skill document, and an edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score. A textual learning-rate budget, rejected-edit buffer, and epoch-wise slow/meta update make skill training stable while adding zero inference-time model calls at deployment. Across six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses (direct chat, Codex, Claude Code), SkillOpt is best or tied on all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells and beats every per-cell competitor among human, one-shot LLM, Trace2Skill, TextGrad, GEPA, and EvoSkill skills. On GPT-5.5 it lifts the average no-skill accuracy by +23.5 points in direct chat, by +24.8 inside the Codex agentic loop, and by +19.1 inside Claude Code. Transfer experiments further show that optimized skill artifacts retain value when moved across model scales, between Codex and Claude Code execution environments, and to a nearby math benchmark without further optimization. We also maintain a [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for released and unreleased changes.** --- ## News 🔥🔥🔥 - **[2026-07-24]** 📰 **SkillOpt in the news.** Read the official [Microsoft Research feature](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/skillopt-agent-skills-as-trainable-parameters/), along with recent coverage from [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/microsofts-open-source-skillopt-automatically-upgrades-ai-agent-skills-without-touching-model-weights), [Synced (机器之心)](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/pMlyj3a3KOh8L7cIHClRXA), [Flowtivity](https://flowtivity.ai/blog/microsoft-skillopt-train-ai-agent-skills/), and [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/microsofts-skillopt-boosts-gpt-5-5-by-using-nothing-but-a-trained-markdown-file/). - **[2026-07-02]** 🚀 **SkillOpt [v0.2.0](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt/releases/tag/v0.2.0) is out on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/skillopt/)!** Headline feature: **SkillOpt-Sleep**, a nightly offline self-evolution engine (harvest → mine → replay → consolidate behind a held-out validation gate), now shipped as the `skillopt-sleep` CLI. It also includes experimental multi-objective, replay, and dream-rollout controls; the main CLI keeps conservative defaults and does not expose every experiment-harness control as a flag. The release source adds integration shells for **Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Devin**, plus an **OpenClaw reference adaptation**; these plugin/MCP files live in the repository rather than the PyPI wheel. It also adds SearchQA split materialization, Windows robustness, and hardened JSON parsing. See the [release notes](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt/releases/tag/v0.2.0) for full release details and contributor acknowledgements. - **[2026-06-15]** 😴 **SkillOpt-Sleep (preview)** — a nightly offline self-evolution companion for local coding agents (Claude Code / Codex / Copilot): review past sessions, replay recurring tasks, and consolidate validated skills behind a held-out gate. See **[`docs/sleep/README.md`](docs/sleep/README.md)** for what it is, how to use it, and results. - **[2026-06-03]** 🎉 **[gbrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain), [gbrain-evals](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain-evals/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/2026-06-03-skillopt.md), and [darwin-skill](https://github.com/alchaincyf/darwin-skill) have all integrated SkillOpt.** - **[2026-06-02]** 🎉 **SkillOpt [v0.1.0](https://github.com/microsoft/SkillOpt/releases/tag/v0.1.0) is now available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/skillopt/)!** Install with `pip install skillopt`. This initial release includes the full training loop (rollout → reflect → aggregate → select → update → evaluate), multi-backend support (OpenAI / Azure / Claude / Qwen / MiniMax), six built-in benchmarks, and WebUI dashboard. --- ## Overview Modern agent skills are usually hand-crafted, generated one-shot by a strong LLM, or evolved through loosely controlled self-revision — none of which behaves like a deep-learning optimizer for the skill itself, and none of which reliably improves over its starting point under feedback. **SkillOpt treats the skill document as the trainable state of a frozen agent**, and trains it with the discipline that makes weight-space optimization reproducible. A separate optimizer model turns scored rollouts into bounded add / delete / replace edits on a single skill document; in the default paper-style path, a candidate edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score. A textual learning-rate budget, a rejected-edit buffer, and an epoch-wise slow / meta update make skill training stable while adding **zero inference-time model calls** at deployment. The deployed artifact is a compact `best_skill.md` (typically 300–2,000 tokens) that runs against the unchanged target model. Across **six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses** (direct chat, Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI), SkillOpt is best or tied-best on **all 52 evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cells** and on GPT-5.5 lifts the average no-skill accuracy by **+23.5 points in direct chat, +24.8 inside the Codex agentic loop, and +19.1 inside Claude Code**. Optimized skill artifacts transfer across model scales, between Codex and Claude Code harnesses, and to nearby benchmarks without further optimization. For the full method, ablations, and per-cell results see the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23904); for a visual walkthrough of the loop see the [project page](https://microsoft.github.io/SkillOpt/); for deeper API / backend / benchmark docs see [`docs/`](docs/). ## 🎬 Demo Video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb12d3bc-371c-467f-904d-91b61f339ed7

▶ Watch the full demo on YouTube

If a provider implements the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol, try the built-in `openai_compatible` backend before adding code. See [`docs/guide/new-backend.md`](docs/guide/new-backend.md) for the full contract. Chat backends add a `skillopt/model/_backend.py` module; target-only exec backends use the shared harness in `codex_harness.py`. Both register through `common.py`, `backend_config.py`, and `skillopt/model/__init__.py`. ### Adding a new benchmark A benchmark = a `skillopt/envs//` package with an adapter, a data loader, a scored rollout helper, a YAML config, and optionally an initial seed skill. The headline of this release is **SkillOpt-Sleep**: a nightly offline
self-evolution engine that harvests a coding agent's real session
transcripts, mines recurring tasks, replays them offline, and consolidates
short-term experience into long-term memory and skills — all behind the same
held-out validation gate that keeps SkillOpt training honest. It ships as a
decoupled top-level package (`skillopt_sleep/`, zero dependency on the
research code) and as the new `skillopt-sleep` CLI.

### Added
- **SkillOpt-Sleep engine** — nightly offline self-evolution cycle
  (harvest → mine → replay → consolidate) behind a validation gate, exposed
  as the `skillopt-sleep` console script and `python -m skillopt_sleep`.
  - Multi-objective reward (accuracy / tokens / latency) with user preferences.
  - Multi-rollout contrastive reflection under a token/time budget.
  - Experience replay + controllable dream rollouts (opt-in).
  - Slow-update long-term memory field (runs even with the gate off).
  - 3-way train/val/test split with `gate_mode on|off`.
  - Verifier-discipline validation gate, with a stress-test suite
    (thanks @Tanmay9223, #87).
- **Cross-tool backends & plugin shells** for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot,
  Devin, and OpenClaw:
  - Codex Desktop transcript harvesting, skill-first Codex integration, and a
    reviewed task-file flow (thanks @Kirchberg, #48, #49, #60).
  - GitHub Copilot backend (`CopilotCliBackend`) + research-engine MCP plugin
    (thanks @Dongbumlee, #50).
  - Devin plugin: MCP server + ATIF-v1.7 harvest (thanks @xerxes-y, #88).
  - OpenClaw shell for SkillOpt-Sleep (thanks @Elzlxx, #59).
- **SearchQA** split materialization helper and fail-fast on systemic rollout
  failures, with a `searchqa` install extra (thanks @summerview1997,
  #63, #64, #65).
- WebUI environment loading and backend preflight (thanks @summerview1997, #63).

- Decoupled the Sleep engine into a standalone top-level `skillopt_sleep/`
  package with zero dependency on the research code.
- Made `EnvAdapter.reflect` a shared default so reflect kwargs are no longer
  dropped (thanks @imshunsuke, #44).
- English-only pass across the engine, plugins, and docs.

- Windows robustness for the Claude/Codex backends, plus a hardened JSON
  fallback path (thanks @Yif-Yang, #79).
- Reject prose pseudo-JSON wrapped in single quotes/backticks (#82).

- Restore `skillopt_webui` to the built wheel (it was dropped when the

     Title: pico-type: A 1.5M-Parameter Byte-Level Multi-Head Content Classifier 
     Authors: Gautam Kishore              View a PDF of the paper titled pico-type: A 1.5M-Parameter Byte-Level Multi-Head Content Classifier, by Gautam Kishore 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: We introduce pico-type, a byte-level multi-head content classifier with approximately 1.5 million parameters that simultaneously predicts seven content properties from raw UTF-8 bytes in a single forward pass. Operating directly at the byte level -- no tokenizer, no subword vocabulary, no pretrained embeddings -- pico-type classifies coarse type (12 classes), modality (8), subtype (24), code language (62), text language (30), file MIME type (90), and risk flags (6-label multi-label: API keys, JWTs, passwords, emails, phone numbers, SSH keys). The architecture combines a learned byte embedding, three convolutional blocks with growing receptive fields, two bidirectional attention layers with rotary position encodings, and a statistical pooling layer feeding seven Matryoshka-style classification heads. Four tiered variants (tiny/small/base/pro) share the same trunk with sliced representations from 16 to 576 dimensions, yielding ONNX exports under 210 KB and CPU inference under 10 ms. Trained on a mixture of synthetic templates and real-world data (8709 GitHub code samples, 5000 Wikipedia articles), pico-type achieves 60.3 percent code language accuracy on The Heap benchmark (24 languages) and 98.2 percent text language accuracy on Wikipedia (30 languages) -- improvements of +57 and +79 percentage points respectively over the synthetic-only baseline. Format-based heads (coarse, modality, subtype, file_mime, risk) maintain 100 percent accuracy on synthetic benchmarks. The model, code, and pretrained weights are released under Apache 2.0.

# pico-type 🔍 **A tiny byte-level multi-head content classifier** — ~1.5M params, ~9MB single-file ONNX (FP32), ~18ms CPU inference. Classifies any content from raw bytes: **coarse type · modality · subtype · code language · text language · file MIME · risk flags** [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-blue)]() [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/pico-type?color=blue)](https://pypi.org/project/pico-type/) [![ONNX](https://img.shields.io/badge/ONNX-exported-success)]() [![CI](https://github.com/eulogik/pico-type/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eulogik/pico-type/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![HuggingFace Space](https://img.shields.io/badge/HuggingFace-Space-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/eulogik/pico-type) [![HuggingFace Model](https://img.shields.io/badge/HuggingFace-Model-orange)](https://huggingface.co/eulogik/pico-type)
--- ## ✨ Features - **No tokenizer** — operates directly on raw UTF-8 bytes (supports all languages, no preprocessing) - **7 heads, one forward pass** — coarse type, modality, subtype, code language, text language, file MIME, risk flags - **4 Matryoshka tiers** — tiny (16d) → small (64d) → base (192d) → pro (576d) — same trunk, accuracy scales with dim - **~9MB single-file ONNX (FP32)** — deploy on edge devices, serverless, browser (WebAssembly/ONNX Runtime Web) - **~18ms inference** on CPU via ONNX Runtime - **CLI, Python API, Gradio Space, MCP server** — ready to use ## 🛡️ ARTH V2 — Risk++ (new) **[Try it live — pick the `arth` model](https://huggingface.co/spaces/eulogik/pico-type)** · [Model files](https://huggingface.co/eulogik/pico-type) (`arth_full_base.onnx`, `risk_thresholds.json`, `temperatures.json`, `arth_final_composite.pt`) Frozen-trunk composite (ft3 student + retrained 14-label **Risk++** head) — audit recall up **5× with zero regressions** on every shipped gate: | Metric | Before (ft3) | ARTH V2 (composite) | |---|---|---| | External-audit positive recall (held-out, never trained/fit on) | 0.107 | **0.536** (60/112) | | Balanced error | 0.459 | **0.260** | | Specificity | 0.961 | 0.944 | | Labels with fitted thresholds | 9 | **14** | | Legacy parity | 60/60 | 60/60 | | Choice accuracy | 0.737 | 0.737 | | Noul abstain | 0.929 | 0.929 | | ToxicChat jailbreak recall / sel-acc@50 | 0.846 / 0.970 | **0.824 / 0.973** (gate PASS) | Formerly-dead labels now detected: jwt / ssh_key / email **8/8**, password 0.875, phone 0.750. Artifact: **`arth_full_base.onnx` (11.66 MB, opset 18)** — auto-verified (torch-vs-ORT err 1.1e-05, parity 60/60, semantic 300/300, risk flags 11/11); INT8 4.28 MB experimental. **Known limitations (measured):** pii_ssn 0.125, api_key 0.625, jailbreak 0.50 on embedded phrasing; 3/11 hand-picked benign probes still flag (incl. the accepted `print('hello world')`→sql); long-document signals dilute in fixed-window pooling; general-classification gates (AG/SST-2/Enron) stay at chance — this is a byte-pattern risk flagger, not a general text classifier. ### ARTH quickstart (ONNX) ```python import json, math import numpy as np, onnxruntime as ort from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download sess = ort.InferenceSession(hf_hub_download("eulogik/pico-type", "arth_full_base.onnx")) thrs = json.load(open(hf_hub_download("eulogik/pico-type", "risk_thresholds.json"))) LABELS = ["api_key","jwt","ssh_key","password","email","phone","prompt_injection", "jailbreak","pii_ssn","pii_card","secrets_aws","secrets_github", "sql_injection","xss_payload"] raw = open("file.txt","rb").read()[:1024] ids = np.zeros(1024, np.int64); ids[:len(raw)] = list(raw) mask = np.zeros(1024, bool); mask[:len(raw)] = True (logits,) = sess.run(["riskpp_logits"], { "input_ids": ids[None,:], "attention_mask": mask[None,:], "opt_embs": np.zeros((1,4,96), np.float32), "struct_feats": np.zeros((1,14), np.float32), "act_stats": np.zeros((1,4), np.float32)}) probs = [1/(1+math.exp(-x)) for x in logits[0]] print({l: round(p,4) for l,p in zip(LABELS, probs) if p >= thrs[l]}) # fired flags ``` ### ARTH quickstart (live Space API) ```python from gradio_client import Client c = Client("eulogik/pico-type") out = c.predict("aws_access_key_id = AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", "arth", api_name="/handle_classify") print(out[7]) # Risk++ (14) tab: probs + [FLAG] markers ``` ## 📊 Evaluation ### Overall Accuracy (v2 — trained on real data) | Head | Classes | Accuracy | Dataset | |------|---------|----------|---------| | coarse | 12 | **100%** | Synthetic eval | | modality | 8 | **100%** | Synthetic eval | | subtype | 24 | **93.8%** | Synthetic eval | | **code_lang** | **62** | **60.3%** | [The Heap](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AISE-TUDelft/the-heap) — 24 real-world langs, 1,200 samples | | **text_lang** | **30** | **98.3%** | [Wikipedia](https://huggingface.co/datasets/wikimedia/wikipedia) — 30 langs, 1,500 samples | | file_mime | 90 | **100%** | Synthetic eval | | risk (mAP) | 6 | **100%** | Synthetic eval | *v0.1 baseline (synthetic-only): code_lang 3%, text_lang 19%. Real-data training in v2 improves code by **57pp** and text by **79pp**.* ### Code Language — Per-Language Accuracy | Excellent (90%+) | Good (70–89%) | Needs Work (<50%) | |---|---|---| | cpp 96%, dart 98%, erlang 98%, rust 98%, r 94%, swift 92%, python 88%, lua 88% | go 86%, ruby 86%, ocaml 84%, php 78%, csharp 76%, java 76%, kotlin 76%, c 62% | perl 50%, haskell 24%, scala 4%, javascript 2%, clojure 0%, elixir 0%, julia 0%, sql 0% | > **Note**: Low-accuracy languages have fewer real training samples. More data will improve them. ## 🚀 Quick Start ### Install ```bash pip install picotype ``` ### CLI ```bash # Classify from stdin echo "def hello(name):\n return f'Hi {name}'" | picotype --pretty # Classify a file picotype --file document.txt # Classify clipboard content picotype --clip # All 4 tiers available echo "..." | picotype --tier pro ``` ### Python API ```python from picotype import load_onnx_model, run_onnx session = load_onnx_model("base") result = run_onnx(session, "def hello(): pass") print(result) # { # "coarse": "code", # "code_language": "python", # "modality": "textual", # "confidence": 0.98, # ... # } ``` ### MCP Server (for Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) ```bash pip install picotype PICOTYPE_MODEL_DIR=./checkpoints python -m model.pico_type.mcp_server ``` Then add to your MCP config: ```json { "mcpServers": { "pico-type": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "model.pico_type.mcp_server"], "env": { "PICOTYPE_MODEL_DIR": "./checkpoints" } } } } ``` ### Gradio Web UI Try it live: [huggingface.co/spaces/eulogik/pico-type](https://huggingface.co/spaces/eulogik/pico-type) ## 🏗 Architecture ``` Bytes ─▶ ByteEmbed(256→96d) ─▶ 3×Conv1D(k=3,5,7) ─▶ 2×BiAttention(RoPE) ─▶ Pool ─▶ 7×Matryoshka Heads ``` | Component | Detail | |-----------|--------| | **ByteEmbed** | Lookup-free embedding — each byte value (0–255) maps to a learned 96-dim vector | | **Conv1D** | 3 parallel depthwise convolutions (kernel widths 3, 5, 7) with residual + layer norm | | **BiAttention** | Bidirectional self-attention with Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), 4 heads | | **Pool** | Mean + max + std deviation concatenation → fixed-size representation | | **Heads** | Matryoshka-style: slice pool dim to 16/64/192/576, project to 7 linear classifiers | Total parameters: **1.43M** (tiny) / **1.45M** (small) / **1.48M** (base) / **1.56M** (pro) ## 🔧 Model Tiers | Tier | Dim | Params | ONNX Size | Accuracy Multiplier | |------|-----|--------|-----------|-------------------| | tiny | 16 | 1.43M | 9.09 MB | 0.65× | | small | 64 | 1.45M | 9.13 MB | 0.82× | | base | 192 | 1.48M | 9.25 MB | 1.0× (reference) | | pro | 576 | 1.56M | 9.61 MB | 1.05× | ONNX sizes are single-file FP32 exports (graph-only files are 203–206 KB). All tiers share the same backbone; only the final linear projection layers differ. Higher-tier models use more dimensions for finer-grained classification. ## 🧪 Classification Heads | Head | Classes | What It Detects | |------|---------|-----------------| | **coarse** | 12 | text, code, link, image, file, config, markup, data, error, secret, archive, binary | | **modality** | 8 | textual, binary_image, binary_archive, binary_executable, binary_document, etc. | | **subtype** | 24 | json, yaml, toml, csv, html, markdown, sql, log, dockerfile, makefile, etc. | | **code_lang** | **62** | python, javascript, typescript, java, c, cpp, go, rust, ruby, php, swift, kotlin, and 50 more | | **text_lang** | 30 | en, es, fr, de, it, pt, nl, ru, zh, ja, ko, vi, th, id, and 15 more | | **file_mime** | **90** | application/json, image/png, video/mp4, font/ttf, application/wasm, and 84 more | | **risk** | 6 | api_key, jwt, password, email, phone, ssh_key | ## 🌐 Deployment | Platform | Link | Notes | |----------|------|-------| | **HuggingFace Space** | [eulogik/pico-type](https://huggingface.co/spaces/eulogik/pico-type) | Gradio web UI, no GPU needed — ARTH V2 + Risk++ (14) by default | | **HuggingFace Model** | [eulogik/pico-type](https://huggingface.co/eulogik/pico-type) | ONNX models + ARTH V2 artifacts (`arth_full_base.onnx`, thresholds, temps, ckpt) | | **GitHub** | [eulogik/pico-type](https://github.com/eulogik/pico-type) | Source code, training, paper | | **PyPI** | `pip install picotype` | Python package | | **ONNX Runtime** | Use with onnxruntime.js | Browser/Node.js deployment | ## 📚 Resources - [Paper (arXiv)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14658) — Architecture, training, and evaluation details - [Paper PDF](paper/main.pdf) — Local copy of the paper - [Model Card](MODEL_CARD.md) — Detailed architecture and training configuration - [Walkthrough](walkthrough.md) — Development log and decisions - [Architecture Plan](docs/PLAN.md) — Original design document ## 📄 License Apache 2.0 ---

     Title: LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders 
     Authors: Shiqiao Gu ,  Yang Yong ,  Fengjun Zhong ,  Ruihao Gong ,  Chengtao Lv ,  Xiangyu Fan ,  Lei Yang ,  Xianglong Liu              View a PDF of the paper titled LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders, by Shiqiao Gu and 7 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Latent diffusion models enable high-quality video generation, but video VAE encoding and decoding remain computationally expensive. Existing methods use stage-specific lightweight operators, yet either constrain spatial and temporal computation jointly or remove temporal computation altogether, without distinguishing their compression sensitivities in pretrained Conv3D. To address these limitations, we present LightVAE, a compression framework that exploits redundancy in temporal modeling and network depth. LightVAE exactly reparameterizes eligible causal Conv3D layers into an aggregate spatial response and a difference-driven temporal correction. Based on their distinct compression sensitivities, temporal low-rank compression (TLR) keeps the aggregate spatial kernel dense and applies layer-specific low-rank approximation only to the temporal correction. An algebraically equivalent folded implementation converts the arithmetic savings into practical acceleration. LightVAE further uses width-preserving block pruning to reduce depth and probe-guided feature alignment, guided by feedback from a frozen teacher suffix, to recover quality after compression. The framework also extends to video encoders. Across three video VAE backbones and two GPU platforms, LightVAE consistently accelerates decoding. For the Wan VAE family, it achieves up to $2.24\times$ and $1.11\times$ the decoding throughput of state-of-the-art efficient VAE decoders on NVIDIA H100 and RTX~5090, respectively, with higher DAVIS PSNR and lower LPIPS. On MiniMax-H3, it achieves up to $2.97\times$ the original decoding throughput while retaining 99.51\% of the original model's overall VBench-2.0 score. Our code is available at  this https URL .

# ⚡ LightVAE **Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders** Wan2.1 · Wan2.2 · MiniMax-H3 [📄 Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14726) · [🤗 Models](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/LightVAE) · [🧩 ComfyUI](comfyui/README.md) · [⚡ LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)
## ✨ Overview **LightVAE** accelerates pretrained video autoencoders while preserving their original latent interfaces. - **Pro** — temporal low-rank compression with the original decoder depth, available for Wan2.1 and Wan2.2. - **Lite** — additional block pruning for Wan; independently pruned encoder and decoder for MiniMax-H3. - **Compatible latents** — compressed components can be paired with their corresponding original components. Wan models retain their original encoders. This repository provides reconstruction examples, decoder benchmarks and H3 ComfyUI workflows. For video generation with LightVAE, see [LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V). ![Architecture comparison](assets/architecture.png) ## 📊 Results Decoder throughput and reconstruction quality reported in **Table 1** of the paper. ![Table 1](assets/table1.png) ## 🎬 Visual Comparisons **NVIDIA H200 · PyTorch 2.11.0 · CUDA 12.8 · BF16** **3 clips × 124 frames · 768p · 24 FPS** Clips are reconstructed separately, then concatenated. Labels show decoder FPS and PSNR; H3 also reports encoder FPS. Timings use eager execution, one warmup and the median of three runs. PSNR is measured before MP4 compression. ### Wan2.1 Left → right: **Original VAE · LightVAE-Pro · LightVAE-Lite** ### Wan2.2 Left → right: **Original VAE · LightVAE-Pro · LightVAE-Lite** ### MiniMax-H3 Left → right: **Original VAE · Lite decoder · Lite encoder + decoder** ## 🧩 ComfyUI · MiniMax-H3 The **Load H3 LightVAE** node reuses ComfyUI’s native H3 VAE. No LightVAE package installation, TLR or custom Triton kernels are needed. - **FL2V:** replace the decoder; keep original first/last-frame encoding. - **REF2V:** replace the encoder, decoder, or both independently. - **`none`:** use the corresponding original component. Audio stays unchanged. - **ConvRot-INT8:** optional quantized Lite decoder; see [download and setup](comfyui/README.md#convrot-int8-decoder). > Use the [installer](comfyui/README.md#install)—do not clone the entire repository directly into `custom_nodes`. Connect the original H3 video VAE to **`base_vae`**, then select Lite components through **Load H3 LightVAE**, not the standard Load VAE node. [Installation guide](comfyui/README.md) · [FL2V workflow](comfyui/workflows/h3_fl2v_lightvae.json) · [Image-reference workflow](comfyui/workflows/h3_ref_image_lightvae.json) · [Video-reference workflow](comfyui/workflows/h3_ref_video_lightvae.json) The current ComfyUI node is **H3-only**. For ComfyUI usage, skip the Python installation below. ## 🛠️ Python Installation Tested with **Python 3.11** and **PyTorch 2.11.0 / CUDA 12.8**. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE.git cd LightVAE python -m pip install -r requirements.txt ``` For model-only installation, use `python -m pip install .`; for development, use `python -m pip install -e ".[cli]"`. ```python from lightvae.wan21_lightvae_decoder import Decoder from lightvae.h3_lightvae_encoder import Encoder ``` Triton is optional for fused Wan kernels and is usually included with NVIDIA Linux PyTorch. H3 uses PyTorch operations; the ComfyUI node uses ComfyUI’s native H3 backend. ## 🤗 Weights Download LightVAE checkpoints: ```bash hf download lightx2v/LightVAE --local-dir weights/LightVAE ``` Use standard, non-INT8 checkpoints with `infer.py` and `benchmark.py`. `lightvae-lite-h3-decoder-int8-convrot.safetensors` is for the ComfyUI node only. Download only the original VAE you need for encoding or baseline comparison: ```bash # Wan2.1 hf download Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B \ Wan2.1_VAE.pth --local-dir weights/Wan2.1 # Wan2.2 TI2V-5B hf download Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B \ Wan2.2_VAE.pth --local-dir weights/Wan2.2 # MiniMax-H3: config and weight shards hf download MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --include "vae/*" --local-dir weights/MiniMax-H3 ``` > **Wan2.2 model selection:** 14B models use the **Wan2.1 VAE**; TI2V-5B uses the **Wan2.2 VAE**. Existing weights can be used directly by passing their paths. ## 🎥 Reconstruction `infer.py` accepts independent **`--encoder`** and **`--decoder`** checkpoints. Examples use BF16 and produce an **MP4 + JSON report** containing PSNR and timings. ### Wan2.1 ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer.py \ --model wan21 --variant lite \ --encoder weights/Wan2.1/Wan2.1_VAE.pth \ --decoder weights/LightVAE/lightvae-lite-wan21-decoder.safetensors \ --input demo.mp4 --frames 81 --height 480 --width 832 \ --output outputs/wan21_lite_recon.mp4 ``` ### Wan2.2 ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer.py \ --model wan22 --variant lite \ --encoder weights/Wan2.2/Wan2.2_VAE.pth \ --decoder weights/LightVAE/lightvae-lite-wan22-decoder.safetensors \ --input demo.mp4 --frames 81 --height 704 --width 1280 \ --output outputs/wan22_lite_recon.mp4 ``` For **Pro**, use `--variant pro` and the corresponding `lightvae-pro-…-decoder.safetensors`. Keep the original encoder. ### MiniMax-H3 **Original encoder + Lite decoder** ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer.py \ --model h3 --variant lite \ --encoder weights/MiniMax-H3/vae \ --decoder weights/LightVAE/lightvae-lite-h3-decoder.safetensors \ --input demo.mp4 --frames 124 --height 768 --width 1344 \ --output outputs/h3_lite_recon.mp4 ``` **Lite encoder + Lite decoder** — no original VAE weights needed for this Python example. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infer.py \ --model h3 --variant lite --encoder-variant lite \ --encoder weights/LightVAE/lightvae-lite-h3-encoder.safetensors \ --decoder weights/LightVAE/lightvae-lite-h3-decoder.safetensors \ --input demo.mp4 --frames 124 --height 768 --width 1344 \ --output outputs/h3_lite_encdec_recon.mp4 ``` **Notes** - For an original baseline, use `--variant base`, pass the original VAE to both component arguments and leave `--encoder-variant base`. - `--frames` limits input length. Omit both size arguments to retain the input resolution; specifying both applies resize-to-cover and center cropping. - PSNR is measured before MP4 compression. Existing output files are not overwritten. ## ⏱️ Decoder Benchmark Compare original and compressed decoders using identical seeded latent inputs. Each decoder runs in a separate process. ```bash # Wan2.1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python benchmark.py \ --model wan21 --weights-dir weights/LightVAE \ --base-weights weights/Wan2.1/Wan2.1_VAE.pth \ --frames 81 --height 480 --width 832 \ --warmup 5 --repeats 30 --output outputs/wan21_speed # Wan2.2 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python benchmark.py \ --model wan22 --weights-dir weights/LightVAE \ --base-weights weights/Wan2.2/Wan2.2_VAE.pth \ --frames 81 --height 704 --width 1280 \ --warmup 5 --repeats 30 --output outputs/wan22_speed # MiniMax-H3 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python benchmark.py \ --model h3 --weights-dir weights/LightVAE \ --base-weights weights/MiniMax-H3/vae \ --frames 124 --height 768 --width 1344 \ --warmup 5 --repeats 30 --output outputs/h3_speed ``` Outputs: **`summary.csv`**, **`summary.json`** and per-decoder logs. Use a new output directory for each run. `--base-weights` specifies the benchmark baseline; it is not an `infer.py` argument. ## 📚 Citation ```bibtex @misc{gu2026lightvae, title={LightVAE: Towards Compact and Efficient Video Autoencoders}, author={Shiqiao Gu and Yang Yong and Fengjun Zhong and Ruihao Gong and Chengtao Lv and Xiangyu Fan and Lei Yang and Xianglong Liu}, year={2026}, eprint={2610.14726}, archivePrefix={arXiv}, primaryClass={cs.CV}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14726} } ``` ## ⭐ Support If you find this useful, please star [LightVAE](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightVAE) and [LightX2V](https://github.com/ModelTC/LightX2V)!

     Title: Small Language Model Makes an Effective Long Text Extractor 
     Authors: Yelin Chen ,  Fanjin Zhang ,  Jie Tang              View a PDF of the paper titled Small Language Model Makes an Effective Long Text Extractor, by Yelin Chen and 2 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a fundamental problem in natural language processing (NLP). However, the task of extracting longer entity spans (e.g., awards) from extended texts (e.g., homepages) is barely explored. Current NER methods predominantly fall into two categories: span-based methods and generation-based methods. Span-based methods require the enumeration of all possible token-pair spans, followed by classification on each span, resulting in substantial redundant computations and excessive GPU memory usage. In contrast, generation-based methods involve prompting or fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to adapt to downstream NER tasks. However, these methods struggle with the accurate generation of longer spans and often incur significant time costs for effective fine-tuning. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a lightweight span-based NER method called SeNER, which incorporates a bidirectional arrow attention mechanism coupled with LogN-Scaling on the [CLS] token to embed long texts effectively, and comprises a novel bidirectional sliding-window plus-shaped attention (BiSPA) mechanism to reduce redundant candidate token-pair spans significantly and model interactions between token-pair spans simultaneously. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art extraction accuracy on three long NER datasets and is capable of extracting entities from long texts in a GPU-memory-friendly manner. # OAG scholar profiling

## Prerequisites

- Linux
- Python 3.7
- PyTorch 1.10.0+cu111

## Getting Started

### Installation

Clone this repo.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/THUDM/scholar-profiling.git
cd scholar-profiling
```

Please install dependencies by

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Dataset

The dataset can be downloaded from [BaiduPan](https://pan.baidu.com/s/1rpwjKInye7ZptmvkmDTPww) (with password 7lro) or Aliyun. There are three parts as follows:
- data_ex.zip [[Aliyun Link]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/data_ex.zip): unzip the file and put the _data_ directory into project directory.
- pretrain_models.zip [[Aliyun Link]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/pretrain_models.zip): unzip the file and put the _pretrain_models_ directory into project directory.
- googleSearch: use _7z_ to extract data.zip in this folder and put the _googleSearch_ directory in the _data_ directory. [[Aliyun Link1]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z01), [[Aliyun Link2]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z02), [[Aliyun Link3]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z03), [[Aliyun Link4]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z04), [[Aliyun Link5]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z05), [[Aliyun Link6]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z06), [[Aliyun Link7]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z07), [[Aliyun Link8]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.z08), [[Aliyun Link9]](https://open-data-set.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/oag-benchmark/scholar-profiling/googleSearch/data.zip)

## How to run
```bash
cd $project_path
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='?'  # specify which GPU(s) to be used
export PYTHONPATH="`pwd`:$PYTHONPATH"

# Statistical machine learning (SML) methods:
# gender
python sml_baseline/GenderPredict/main.py
# homepage
python sml_baseline/HomepagePrediction/homepage_train.py
# position
python sml_baseline/TitlePrediction/title_main.py
# evaluation
python sml_baseline/merge_results.py
python evaluate.py --hp output/sml/sml_predict_xgboost.json --rf data/raw/ground_truth.json

# BERT
# First, uncomment three functions including create_gender_classification_data(), create_homepage_classification_data(), create_title_classification_data() to generate training data
python bert_baseline/tools.py 
# gender
python bert_baseline/gender_classification_bert.py
# homepage
python bert_baseline/homepage_classification_bert.py
# position
python bert_baseline/title_classification_bert.py
# for evaluation, uncomment merge_result() funciton in bert_baseline/tools.py 
python bert_baseline/tools.py 
python evaluate.py --hp data/luoyang-result_new.json --rf data/raw/ground_truth.json

# Bi-LSTM-CRF for position tagging
python data_process.py
python bert_bilstm_crf/run.py

# BERT with prompt tuning
# First, uncomment four functions including get_gender_data(r'data/raw/new_dev.xlsx'), get_title_data(r'data/raw/new_dev.xlsx'), get_gender_test(), and get_train_data() to generate training data
python data_process.py
# gender
python prompt/gender_prompt.py
# postion
python prompt/title_prompt.py

```

For how to extract more attributes from long texts of scholars' profiles, please see README.md in `bio_models`.
